recreation_brief: 1. Set slide background to white and draw a thin red (#C62828) rectangle framing the entire slide edge. 2. Add a light gray (#E0E0E0) header band across the top (~15% height). 3. In the header, place green (#4CAF50) doodle icons (notebook + coffee cup) at left, then the bold red title 'Data Representation' in large sans-serif. 4. Add a yellow (#FFF59D) circle with black text '25' at the top-right corner. 5. Draw a thin red-bordered white content box below the header occupying most of the slide. 6. Inside, add three round-bullet items in black sans-serif: 'Data has form: {(x₁ , y₁ ), . . . , (x_N , y_N )} (labeled), or {x₁ , . . . , x_N } (unlabeled)'; 'Each example X is a set of (numeric) features / attributes / dimensions' (bold the word 'features'); 'X is commonly represented as a D × 1 vector'. 7. Under the third bullet, add two dash sub-bullets: 'Representing a 28 × 28 image: x can be a 784 × 1 vector of pixel values' and 'Representing a text document: x can be a vector of word-counts of words appearing in that document'. 8. Use subscript formatting for x₁, y₁, x_N, y_N.
